evidence.claim: A working Worker fetch handler that imports functions/api/chat.js and functions/api/contact.js directly as ES modules and invokes their onRequestPost/onRequestOptions exports with a hand-shimmed Pages-Functions-shaped context object.

This is a correction of this evidence entry's original wording (see migration-risk.json) — the direct-import approach works here (proven live, CF-C1-C4) only because functions/ is trivially simple (2 flat files, no nesting), and it is also the confirmed root cause of the security-header gap in repo-vs-live.md, since the hand-rolled entrypoint never imports functions/_middleware.js the way the official compile step would have.

evidence.claim: No _routes.json file exists anywhere in this repository.
evidence.relevance: Per CF-A9, a Pages project with Functions and no _routes.json invokes a Function on EVERY request, including static assets — meaning a live Pages deployment of this exact repo as-configured would not get free/unlimited static requests at all. This is new, decision-relevant economic evidence not present in the first-pass decision.

evidence.claim: Free: 100,000 req/day, 10ms CPU/HTTP request, 128MB memory, 50 subrequests/request, 6 simultaneous connections, 64 env vars/Worker, 3MB gzipped Worker size, 20,000 static asset files, 25MiB individual asset. Paid: no request limit, 5min CPU ceiling, 128MB memory, 10,000 subrequests/request, 128 env vars, 10MB Worker size, 100,000 static asset files, 25MiB individual asset (unchanged).
evidence.relevance: None of these limits realistically constrain a single dental-practice site: Smile Savers' functions/ handlers are tiny (well under 3MB), issue at most 1-2 subrequests each (Resend/Workers AI calls), and dist/ has nowhere near 20,000 files (32 pages + assets, confirmed by npm run build output this session).

evidence.claim: "On a purely static project, Pages offers unlimited free requests. However, once you add Functions on a Pages project, all requests by default will invoke your Function." A _routes.json with at least one include rule is required to exclude static paths from Function invocation and keep them free; exclude rules take priority over include rules; max 100 combined rules.
evidence.relevance: Directly falsifies an implicit assumption in the first-pass decision that Pages' static-asset economics are automatically as good as Workers'. They are NOT, once Functions exist, without an explicit _routes.json — which this repo does not have (REPO-B4).

evidence.source: Cloudflare Migrate from Pages to Workers (developers.cloudflare.com/workers/static-assets/migrate-from-pages/)
evidence.claim: "If you use Pages Functions with a folder of functions/, you must first compile these functions into a single Worker script with the wrangler pages functions build command" (npx wrangler pages functions build --outdir=./dist/worker/). Workers Static Assets serves matching static files BEFORE the Worker script by default, unless assets.run_worker_first is set. Both _headers and _redirects are natively supported under Workers Static Assets, same as Pages.
evidence.relevance: Corrects the first-pass decision's claim that no compilation step is needed in general (see REPO-B2's correction) — Cloudflare's own recommended path does require it; confirms _headers/_redirects portability (explains CF-C1's finding); confirms run_worker_first is a non-issue for Smile Savers' current two flat API routes (neither matches a static file path).
